Yen's Q3 residual correlations

Source: R/local_dependence.R
RMlocdepQ3.Rd

Computes Yen's \(Q_3\), the correlations between the model residuals of each pair of items, to assess local dependence. By default the item parameters are estimated by conditional maximum likelihood and the person locations by WLE (estimator = "CML"). With the result of RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(), it also tests each pair against simulations, by default with a bootstrap p-value corrected across pairs.

Usage

RMlocdepQ3(
  data,
  cutoff = NULL,
  output = "kable",
  n_pairs = NULL,
  p_value = NULL,
  correction = c("fwer", "fdr_bh", "fdr_by", "none"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  estimator = c("CML", "MML")
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Missing values (NA) are allowed. \(Q_3\) is computed from the respondents who answered both items of a pair, and respondents with no responses are dropped.

cutoff

Optional. Either of:

  • NULL (default): the \(Q_3\) matrix.

  • A single number: the matrix with a global dynamic cutoff, the mean off-diagonal \(Q_3\) plus this number (for example suggested_cutoff from RMlocdepQ3Cutoff()).

  • The full result of RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(): a list of two tables, the matrix with the global cutoff and a table per pair (see Value).

output

Character. "kable" (default) for knitr::kable() tables, or "dataframe".

n_pairs

Integer or NULL (default). With the full cutoff object, shows only the n_pairs pairs that depart most from their expected range in the pair table. NULL shows all pairs. The correction always covers all pairs.

p_value

Logical or NULL. Whether to flag pairs on one-sided bootstrap p-values (p_q3, padj_q3) for excess positive dependence. NULL (default) uses them whenever cutoff is the full RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() result, so a numeric cutoff or none keeps the interval. FALSE gives the behaviour before version 1.2.0. The interval describes where a pair's \(Q_3\) is expected to fall. Used as a decision rule over m pairs, a width w gives a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^m, and the number of pairs grows with the square of the number of items (Johansson, 2026).

correction

Character. Correction of the p-values across all pairs: "fwer" (default, Westfall-Young step-down), "fdr_bh" or "fdr_by" (Benjamini-Hochberg or Benjamini-Yekutieli), or "none".

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). A pair is flagged when its corrected p-value is below alpha. Default 0.05. Used only with p-values.

estimator

Character. How the residuals are computed. "CML" (default) uses CML item parameters (psychotools) and WLE person locations, which are finite at extreme scores. "MML" uses marginal maximum likelihood and EAP (mirt), kept for older analyses. It must match the estimator of RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(). With the full cutoff object, its stored estimator is used, with a warning if estimator differs.

Value

With cutoff = NULL or a number, one table (knitr_kable or data.frame) with the lower triangle of the \(Q_3\) matrix. A number adds a flag for pairs above the dynamic cutoff and a caption describing it.

With the full RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() result, a named list:

matrix

the \(Q_3\) matrix with the global dynamic cutoff (mean off-diagonal \(Q_3\) plus suggested_cutoff), as above.

pairs

one row per item pair with Item1, Item2, Observed (\(Q_3\)), Low and High (the pair's simulated interval) and Flagged: "above" (above the interval, local dependence), "below" or "". Sorted by the departure from the pair's simulated median and cut to n_pairs. With p-values, also p_q3 and padj_q3, and Flagged marks padj_q3 < alpha, only as "above".

The \(Q_3\) heatmap is drawn by RMlocdepQ3Plot() (its matrix element), so the tables and plots share the matrix and pairs structure.

Details

Statistic. \(Q_3\) (Yen, 1984) is the correlation between the residuals of two items after the latent variable is accounted for. Under local independence it is around \(-1/(k-1)\) for k items. With a cutoff, the dynamic cutoff is the mean of all off-diagonal \(Q_3\) plus cutoff (Christensen et al., 2017).

Estimation. \(Q_3\) is the correlation matrix of the standardized residuals \((x - E)/\sqrt{Var}\). With "MML" the residuals come from mirt. The two estimators give very similar \(Q_3\) (the off-diagonal values typically correlate above .95). What matters for inference is that the observed \(Q_3\) and the simulations in RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() use the same estimator, which the functions enforce.

Two views. With the full RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() result, two tables are returned. matrix applies one global cutoff, the 99th percentile of the simulated maximum minus mean \(Q_3\) (Christensen et al., 2017), an overview of whether there is any local dependence. pairs compares each observed \(Q_3\) with its own simulated interval, so that single dependent pairs can be read off and ranked.

Bootstrap p-values. Each observed \(Q_3\) is tested against its simulated values (cutoff$pair_results), one-sided for excess local dependence. The statistic is the deviation from the mean of the observed and simulated values together, divided by their SD. The uncorrected p is (1 + #{Q3* >= Q3}) / (B + 1) for B simulated datasets, and correction adjusts across the \(k(k-1)/2\) pairs (Westfall-Young step-down, Ferreira, 2024, or FDR). As for item fit, the family-wise error rate is controlled at any number of iterations, but decisions depend on the seed. Below 400 iterations a message says so once per session, and between 400 and 1000 the caption notes it. A false discovery rate correction needs far more iterations than the family-wise one, since a bootstrap p-value cannot fall below 1/(B + 1) and Benjamini-Hochberg compares the smallest with alpha/m. Over the 36 pairs of a nine-item scale that takes 720 iterations, and over the 190 pairs of a twenty-item scale 3799, against 19 for Westfall-Young whatever the number of pairs.

Multiple comparisons

The uncorrected p-value controls the error rate of a single comparison. For one item (or item pair) chosen in advance it is the relevant value. Flagging whichever of k comparisons fall below alpha tests k hypotheses at once, and the chance of at least one false flag rises to about \(1 - (1 - \alpha)^k\), for example 34% for k = 8 at alpha = 0.05, even when every uncorrected p-value is calibrated. The corrected p-value controls this. correction = "fwer" bounds the probability of any false flag (strict, less power), and "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" bound the expected share of false flags among those raised. Use the uncorrected p-value for a single comparison chosen in advance, and a corrected one when screening the whole table, which is the usual case.

References

Christensen, K. B., Makransky, G., & Horton, M. (2017). Critical values for Yen's \(Q_3\): Identification of local dependence in the Rasch model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 41(3), 178–194. doi:10.1177/0146621616677520

Ferreira, J. A. (2024). Methods of testing a 'small' or 'moderate' number of hypotheses simultaneously. Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice, 19(1), 6. doi:10.1007/s42519-024-00412-4

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

Yen, W. M. (1984). Effects of local item dependence on the fit and equating performance of the three-parameter logistic model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 8(2), 125–145. doi:10.1177/014662168400800201

See also

RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() for the simulations, RMlocdepQ3Plot() for the plots, RMlocdepGamma() for partial gamma.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Simulate binary item response data (10 items, 200 persons)
set.seed(42)
sim_data <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
)
colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

# Raw Q3 matrix (no cutoff)
RMlocdepQ3(sim_data)
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Raw Q3 residual correlations (lower triangle). Use RMlocdepQ3Cutoff() to derive a cutoff. n = 200 respondents.
#> 
#> |       |Item1 |Item2 |Item3 |Item4 |Item5 |Item6 |Item7 |Item8 |Item9 |Item10 |
#> |:------|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:------|
#> |Item1  |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item2  |-0.02 |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item3  |-0.17 |-0.2  |      |      |      |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item4  |-0.13 |-0.2  |-0.1  |      |      |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item5  |-0.19 |-0.06 |-0.02 |-0.12 |      |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item6  |-0.1  |-0.1  |-0.17 |0.03  |-0.19 |      |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item7  |-0.17 |-0.13 |-0.07 |0.03  |-0.04 |-0.11 |      |      |      |       |
#> |Item8  |-0.03 |-0.06 |-0.11 |-0.28 |-0.05 |-0.16 |-0.18 |      |      |       |
#> |Item9  |-0.03 |-0.08 |-0.16 |-0.19 |-0.22 |-0.03 |-0.1  |-0.02 |      |       |
#> |Item10 |-0.16 |-0.14 |0     |-0.09 |-0.1  |-0.18 |-0.15 |-0.12 |-0.09 |       |

# Get the underlying data.frame
q3_df <- RMlocdepQ3(sim_data, output = "dataframe")

# Simulation-based cutoff (use 1000 or more iterations in real analyses)
if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cutoff_res <- RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(sim_data, iterations = 50, parallel = FALSE)

  # A single number gives the matrix only
  RMlocdepQ3(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res$suggested_cutoff)

  # The full object gives two tables, $matrix and $pairs
  res <- RMlocdepQ3(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, output = "dataframe")
  res$pairs

  # Top 5 pairs, with bootstrap p-values (use iterations >= 1000 in practice)
  RMlocdepQ3(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, n_pairs = 5, p_value = TRUE,
             output = "dataframe")$pairs
}
